clue.text: Peninsula where I live has elevated appearance

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: in a down clue, something elevated is lifted so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a manner or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone describes the peninsula they call home as having a lofty look.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmass holding Spain and Portugal is a peninsula of south-west Europe.

clue.text: Vessel wants power in a Brazilian city

indicators.note: the word for power goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a boat is a vessel
vis is Latin for force or power

explanation.surface: A ship needs more engine power when it reaches a Brazilian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Boa Vista is the capital of the northern Brazilian state of Roraima.

clue.text: Buckle seen on this item of footwear

indicators.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape, so the following letters are distorted

explanation.surface: A buckle has been spotted on this shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckle' looks like a noun for a shoe fastening but signals the anagram of SEEN ON THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sports shoe, the kind worn on a court, is an item of footwear.

clue.text: Partners getting a grand in payment

indicators.note: the partners get the letters put between them

parts.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Couples are being paid a thousand each.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge W and E (West and East) play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay received for work done is a payment.

clue.text: Property value around a steel works?

indicators.note: the value word sits around the rest

parts.note: a rate is a value or price

indicators.note: works as a verb means is worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a steelworks site is worth as property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'value around' reads as a valuation of a site, but 'works' is the anagram signal and 'around' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings are property, the subject of a realtor's trade.

clue.text: 50% reduction — a record

indicators.note: fifty per cent asks for half of the word, its first half here

parts.note: a discount is a reduction in price

explanation.surface: A record is on sale at half price.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record is a flat disc of grooved plastic.

clue.text: See you playing alone, knocking one off

indicators.note: knocking something off removes it, here the letter for one
with knocking, says that a letter is taken away

parts.note: a musician playing alone is soloing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a musician playing solo after knocking off a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal farewells said on parting.

clue.text: Breastplate, or plate designed to cover top of chest

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover, that is go around, the chosen letter
letters designed afresh are rearranged
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: An armourer offers a breastplate or a plate made to protect the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' makes PETORAL, which 'to cover' wraps around the letter C taken by 'top of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pectoral is an ornamental plate worn on the chest, as by a Jewish high priest.

clue.text: Securities firm bankrupt, leading to fury

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: broke means penniless
rage is fury

explanation.surface: A finance company goes bust and investors are furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that buys and sells shares for clients is a stockbroking business.

clue.text: Single and zero combined

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
none is zero

explanation.surface: One and nothing are put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Things brought into one unit, as in an all-purpose gadget, are joined together.

clue.text: Be sorry about steady profit

indicators.note: the regret word goes about the other piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret
even means steady, regular

explanation.surface: A trader regrets that profits have merely held steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Income brought in by a business is its takings, loosely its profit.

clue.text: TUC look worried by management reaction to strike

indicators.note: worried letters are fretted and shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Union leaders look anxious as bosses respond to a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Shutting workers out of the workplace is an employer's counter-move in a dispute.

clue.text: Promotions which Nasdaq holds over

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards
the word Nasdaq holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Advertising on the American stock exchange is turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' picks SDA from inside Nasdaq; 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverts promote products, so short adverts are promotions.

clue.text: Business record good, leaderless organisation admits

indicators.note: the rearranged letters let the next piece in
an organisation of letters is an arranging of them

explanation.surface: A company without a boss keeps a good set of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like the company, but rearranges LEADERLESS, which 'admits' G.
explanation.definitionFit: The book of accounts recording money owed by customers is a business record.

clue.text: Who stops trading £51 for gold?

parts.note: 51 is LI in Roman numerals and a pound is a quid
at as in at a price, for a price
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A riddle asks who would give up commerce for fifty-one pounds in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Read £51 as 51 then the pound: LI then QUID.
explanation.definitionFit: An official appointed to wind up a company ends its business.

clue.text: Business community, after IT sell-off, reversed effect of pricing?

indicators.note: the business word comes after the turned pieces
the two pieces before it are read backwards together

parts.note: a sale is a sell-off
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: The financial world rethinks after a technology share dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Price elasticity is how demand responds to price changes, an effect of pricing.

clue.text: Onset of ruin in finance?

indicators.note: the letter goes in the money word

parts.note: cash is money, finance

indicators.note: the onset is the start, the first letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about the start of financial ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A market collapse is the start of ruin in finance.

clue.text: Initially confused, go and falsify business account

indicators.note: the initial letters of the two words are mixed up, swapped

parts.note: to have a bash is to have a go
to cook the books is to falsify them

explanation.surface: A muddled clerk sets about falsifying the company accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: BASH and COOK swap their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger of cash received and paid out is a business account book.

clue.text: 3/4 of a yard, as in Latin

indicators.note: keeping three quarters of a four-letter word means dropping its final letter

parts.note: a ..., or quadrangle, is a college yard

explanation.surface: A measurement fraction meets a Latin grammar note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yard' looks like the unit of length, but it is a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Qua is a Latin word meaning in the capacity of, used in English.

clue.text: Financier's City location

definitions.meaning: a backer who funds a new venture or a stage show
a district of Islington in north London, with its own Underground station

explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy investor in a show is a backer; Angel is also a London area.

clue.text: Defend soldier's denial, with temper rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading bottom to top

parts.note: a soldier says no sir when refusing
to lose your rag is to lose your temper

explanation.surface: A soldier hotly denies wrongdoing and defends himself in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NO SIR RAG upward. 'Lose one's rag' is British slang for losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To garrison a town is to station troops in it to defend it.

clue.text: Obvious fault in life-vest containing hole?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters contain the next piece
a faulty life-vest is broken, its letters disarranged

parts.note: a den is a hole, a lair

explanation.surface: A defect in a life jacket is clear, since it has a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' makes SELFEVIT from LIFE-VEST, which holds DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain without needing proof, so obvious.

clue.text: Loan shark causing slight capital loss?

indicators.note: losing the capital is losing the first letter

parts.note: slender means slight

explanation.surface: A moneylender makes a small loss on the capital he lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital loss' looks like finance jargon but drops the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark is an extortionate one who lends money.

clue.text: Starts to refill old brown mug

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone refills an old brown mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' is the verb: to mug someone is to rob them.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug someone is to rob them violently in the street.

clue.text: One could make a fool out of northern capitalist

indicators.note: the baker word is put outside the letter

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream dessert, which a baker might make

explanation.surface: Someone from the north makes a fool of a financier.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit and cream; 'make a fool out of' pretends to mean humiliate.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker deals in capital, so is a capitalist.

clue.text: A fat cat recalled grabbing a country's sudden wealth

indicators.note: the turned letters grab the others inside
called back, so read backwards

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy toff
NZ is New Zealand

explanation.surface: A greedy rich man takes hold of a nation's windfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns A NOB to BONA, which grabs A NZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a sudden windfall of riches.

clue.text: Form of money that's anything but Euro

parts.note: anything but means not
E is short for European

explanation.surface: A type of money that is not the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is paper money.

clue.text: Selling of university hampered by lawsuit

indicators.note: the lawsuit has the letter stuck within it

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A university sale is held up by litigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale by competitive bids is a form of selling.

clue.text: Parliaments pass them while obstructing court

indicators.note: the court letters block the middle of the other word

parts.note: as means while

explanation.surface: Parliaments push laws through while the courts get in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws enacted by a legislature are statutes.

clue.text: This is not hard to see in spare time

parts.note: over means left over, spare

explanation.surface: Something easily seen during leisure hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open and unconcealed is plainly visible.

clue.text: Our test fails to keep good piston movement

indicators.note: the jumbled letters keep the next piece inside
a test that fails breaks down, its letters jumbled

parts.note: OK means good

explanation.surface: An engineer's trial of a piston fails yet still passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' makes OUTSTRE from OUR TEST, keeping OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The outward stroke of a piston in a cylinder is a piston movement.
